reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports that moderate negative misfit at γ/γ′ interfaces impedes dislocations and improves creep resistance in HESAs, and that the misfit-creep relationship is non-monotonic. However, the evidence is from bulk high-entropy superalloys with precipitates, not from engineered multilayer coatings, so the direct support for the specific premise that alternating HEA layers with controlled misfit will reduce creep in coatings is an extrapolation not directly evidenced.
premises: Moderate lattice misfit at interfaces impedes dislocation motion
Moderate lattice misfit reduces atomic diffusion
A negative lattice misfit is more effective in resisting creep
The relationship between misfit magnitude and creep resistance is non-monotonic
Multilayer interfaces with misfit will reduce steady-state creep rate vs. homogeneous coating
